successCriteria.description: All five error classes (NotFoundError, ValidationError, ConflictError, UnauthorizedError, ForbiddenError) extend Error and are exported from src/shared/errorTypes.ts, each setting this.name to its own class name.

NotFoundError exposes readonly resourceName and resourceId string properties; ConflictError exposes readonly resourceName; ValidationError exposes readonly details as a string array — all preserved after instantiation with the values passed to the constructor.
Each error instance carries a defined stack trace that contains the class name, demonstrating Error.captureStackTrace was invoked (guarded so it does not throw on runtimes lacking the API).

The Jest unit test suite in tests/unit/shared/errorTypes.test.ts verifies every error class instantiates correctly, preserves its message and custom properties, and captures a stack trace — and the suite passes under the ts-jest node environment.

constraints: No use of `any` — typed error classes must use concrete types (string, string[]) for their custom properties, consistent with the no-any rule in HARNESS.json.
Error.captureStackTrace must be guarded (e.g. `if (Error.captureStackTrace)`) so the module does not throw on runtimes where the API is absent.
The module must compile under strict TypeScript (strict null checks, no implicit any) targeting ES2022/commonjs as configured in tsconfig.json.
This phase has zero dependencies on prior phases — errorTypes.ts must not import from any leave module or other domain code; it is a shared utility consumed by later phases.
outOfScope: HTTP status mapping logic (404/400/409/401/403) — the error classes only define the types; controllers in Phase 7 perform the status mapping.
Consumption of these error classes by the leave service (Phase 6) or controller (Phase 7) — this phase only defines and tests the shared types.
Auth middleware and JWT utilities (Phase 5) — UnauthorizedError and ForbiddenError are defined here as types only; their enforcement via middleware is a later phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: Every instance is an Error subclass whose name is exactly 'NotFoundError' and whose resourceName and resourceId are immutable after construction.
Every instance is an Error subclass whose name is exactly 'ValidationError' and whose details array is immutable after construction.
Every instance is an Error subclass whose name is exactly 'ConflictError' and whose resourceName is immutable after construction.
Every instance is an Error subclass whose name is exactly 'UnauthorizedError' with no custom properties beyond the Error message.
Every instance is an Error subclass whose name is exactly 'ForbiddenError' with no custom properties beyond the Error message.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Constructing any of the five error classes with a message string (and class-specific payload) produces a throwable Error whose name and custom properties are set; construction never throws for valid string inputs.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Construction itself does not raise; the resulting object is intended to be thrown by callers and caught at API boundaries.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Error.captureStackTrace invocation during construction — must be guarded so that runtimes without the API do not throw; when available it captures the stack excluding the constructor frame.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: If Error.captureStackTrace is undefined, construction proceeds normally without a stack-capture failure.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The five error classes and their custom properties must match the shared error-types table in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: NotFoundError (resourceName, resourceId → 404), ValidationError (details → 400), ConflictError (resourceName → 409), UnauthorizedError (→ 401), ForbiddenError (→ 403).

The test file must import all five error classes from the canonical module location src/shared/errorTypes.ts and verify instantiation, property preservation, and stack-trace capture for each — matching the existing test coverage.

integrationPoints.target: Leave service (Phase 6) — will throw NotFoundError, ConflictError, ForbiddenError, and ValidationError to signal domain rule violations.
integrationPoints.why: These typed errors are the canonical failure vocabulary the service layer uses for state-machine guards and ownership checks.

integrationPoints.target: Leave controller (Phase 7) — will catch these typed errors and map them to HTTP status codes (404/400/409/401/403).
integrationPoints.why: The controller's try/catch error-mapping logic depends on instanceof checks against these exact class names.

integrationPoints.target: Auth middleware (Phase 5) — will throw UnauthorizedError and ForbiddenError for authentication and RBAC failures.
integrationPoints.why: GP-005 (RBAC enforcement) and auth failures surface through these shared error types at API boundaries.
